question: Who is winning, and how much time remains?
data: plays: preSnapHomeScore, preSnapVisitorScore, quarter, gameClock; games: team abbreviations
method: Display the score and clock recorded before the selected play. Join games by gameId to label home/away.
limitation: No timeout counts, play clock, continuous live clock or explicit final score. Do not treat the next selected row as the next actual play.

question: How far does the team need to advance?
data: plays: down, yardsToGo, absoluteYardlineNumber; tracking: playDirection
method: Draw the start line and target line: target_x = line_x + sign * yardsToGo, with sign +1 right or -1 left. Clip the target to the opponent goal line. Display down and yards remaining.
limitation: Reaching the target with an off-ball receiver is not earning a first down. Detect goal-to-go from field position; validate penalties separately.

question: Where does this play start?
data: plays: yardlineSide, yardlineNumber, absoluteYardlineNumber; tracking: playDirection
method: Draw the line at absoluteYardlineNumber and label the team's yard line. Normalize left-going plays if desired.
limitation: One play has missing absoluteYardlineNumber. Recover from validated field metadata or mark unavailable; do not replace with zero.

question: Which player should I watch?
data: tracking: nflId, jerseyNumber, team; players: displayName, officialPosition; scouting: pff_role
method: Join names and roles; let the creator click a player, add a ring and show name/jersey/role.
limitation: Roles are specific to each play. The ball has no nflId and is not a player.

question: What just happened?
data: tracking: frameId, x, y, event; plays: playDescription, passResult, playResult
method: Animate dots on a field; add creator-controlled pause, scrub, trails and annotations. Present recorded outcome as a separate replay summary.
limitation: No video supplied. Sample tracking stops around release, so show the actual endpoint and do not invent a catch animation.

question: What have I missed?
data: plays: playDescription, gameClock, quarter, passResult, playResult
method: Create a browseable list of selected passing plays, filtered by game and outcome.
limitation: Dataset omits designed runs and special teams; it cannot reconstruct complete drives or a full game recap.

question: Was the receiver open?
data: tracking: x, y, team, frameId; scouting: pff_role = Pass Route; plays: defensiveTeam
method: For a selected route runner, compute distance to every opposing defender at the same frame and display the minimum. Highlight the nearest defender.
limitation: Call this nearest-defender distance, not catch probability or proof of openness. No threshold is a universal safe-pass rule.

question: How did the receiver get open?
data: tracking: x, y, frameId; scouting: pff_role
method: Show the receiver's observed path and nearby defenders' paths from snap to the selected frame. Pair with changing separation.
limitation: Explains movement, not a definitive cause. Route names such as slant are not provided; do not label automatically without a validated classifier or manual review.

question: When did space appear or disappear?
data: tracking: frameId, x, y; scouting: roles
method: Plot nearest-defender distance per frame; sync a cursor to the replay. Optionally show the gap change over the preceding 0.5 seconds.
limitation: The nearest defender can change; include its identity. A gap change is not the same as that defender's speed toward the receiver.

question: Could the quarterback have thrown to someone else?
data: tracking: all player coordinates; scouting: Pass and Pass Route roles
method: Freeze at pass_forward and show each route runner's nearest-defender distance and location relative to the first-down target.
limitation: No reliable target ID, QB gaze, intended progression, ball height or calibrated throwing-lane model. Present alternatives to discuss, not a best-target verdict.

question: Was that a difficult completion?
data: Available: outcome, coverage, formation and pre-release spacing; missing: clean target ID and calibrated probability model
method: Use a descriptive card for throw timing and spacing today. A future probability model needs target labels, training data, game-held-out validation and calibration.
limitation: A logistic model with arbitrary weights or a separation-to-percent conversion would not reproduce NFL completion probability.

question: Is the quarterback completing unusually difficult passes?
data: plays: passResult; scouting: Pass role; missing: expected completion probability per attempt
method: Actual completion percentage can be calculated for C/I/IN attempts only. CPOE needs an independently validated expectation for those same attempts.
limitation: Exclude sacks, scrambles and nullified plays from official pass attempts; review penalty-affected records. Do not call actual completion percentage CPOE or full-season performance.

question: How far did the pass travel before the catch?
data: Missing consistent catch/arrival location and receiver target ID; release-side player positions exist
method: A simpler available graphic is receiver depth at release: direction-adjusted receiver_x minus start-line_x.
limitation: Receiver depth at release is not air yards. playResult includes yards after the catch and sometimes penalties; it is not air yards either.

question: How much did the receiver gain after catching it?
data: Missing consistent catch frame, ball carrier ID and end-of-play tracking; plays has total result
method: Add official play-by-play receiving/air-yard fields or full post-catch tracking before calculating YAC.
limitation: Only one catch event and no tackle events in the 181-play tracking sample. Do not treat total play yards as YAC.

question: Did the receiver gain more after the catch than expected?
data: Requires actual YAC, catch-time context and an expected-YAC model
method: Supplement post-catch data, train and calibrate an expectation, then compare actual minus expected.
limitation: Both the core outcome breakdown and model are missing.

question: Is the quarterback repeatedly throwing into tight coverage?
data: Missing clean target identity and catch/incompletion-time separation
method: Manually annotate a few intended receivers and show their separation at release as a separate descriptive feature.
limitation: That would be a release-time measure, not the established NGS tight-window metric. Do not silently substitute the timing or denominator.

question: Who is getting the ball most?
data: plays: playDescription, passResult; players: displayName; no targetedReceiverId
method: Manually label targets on selected demo plays, or join a public play-by-play target/receiver field for broader counts.
limitation: Names in descriptions need disambiguation; Pass Route means running a route, not being targeted. Do not count all route runners as targets.

question: Was the failed pass caused by the throw, receiver or defender?
data: plays: passResult, playDescription; scouting: hurry/hit flags; pre-release tracking
method: Show the recorded outcome and whether PFF credited a hurry or hit, with the actual movement replay.
limitation: No drop or pass-breakup fields and little catch-time evidence. Avoid automated blame or causal claims.

question: How long did the quarterback take to throw?
data: tracking: event, frameId; scouting: pff_role = Pass
method: (pass_forward frame - ball_snap frame) / 10. Show an elapsed timer and a release marker.
limitation: Use annotated events preferentially; autoevent labels may disagree. Sacks have no release and should not receive a fabricated throw time. Exported time strings are whole-second precision.

question: Why did the quarterback have to rush his throw?
broadcast: Pressure graphics and pressure / hit statistics
data: scouting: pff_hurry, pff_hit; tracking: passer/rusher positions
method: Show PFF-credited hurry/hit on the play, then replay the credited defender's approach and snap-to-release time.
limitation: The labels describe the play afterward and have no precise onset frame. They do not prove why the QB released.

question: Was the quarterback's protection collapsing?
data: tracking: passer, blockers, rushers; scouting: role and pressure flags
method: Display QB-to-nearest-pass-rusher distance over time, with blocker and rusher trails.
limitation: This is a descriptive distance display, not Amazon Pocket Health. Distance ignores intervening blockers and cannot by itself determine pressure.

question: Which defender beat his blocker?
broadcast: Pass-rush win rate and isolated replay
data: scouting: pff_nflIdBlockedPlayer, pff_beatenByDefender, pff_hitAllowed, pff_hurryAllowed, pff_sackAllowed
method: Connect each blocking player's first recorded assignment to the defender and show PFF's credited outcome. Use the trails for explanation.
limitation: First assignment is not a continuous matchup. These labels do not replicate ESPN's timing-based pass-rush win rate.

question: Which blocker protected the quarterback well?
broadcast: Pass-block win rate and pressure allowed
data: scouting: role, block type, pressure-allowed flags and first blocked player
method: Show blocker participation and recorded hit/hurry/sack allowed, with replay. Aggregate only over matching eligible blocking plays.
limitation: A zero flag does not establish a great block. Do not relabel these counts as ESPN pass-block win rate or a PFF grade.

question: Did the quarterback cause the sack by holding the ball too long?
data: tracking: snap, qb_sack, positions; plays: passResult S; scouting: sack and sackAllowed
method: For plays with a sack marker, show snap-to-sack time, receiver spacing before it and credited sack/allowed labels.
limitation: This supplies context, not responsibility. Do not infer a missed passing opportunity solely from distance.

question: Are defenders following receivers or guarding areas?
data: plays: pff_passCoverageType and pff_passCoverage
method: Display PFF's Man, Zone or Other label with the more specific recorded scheme and a short explanation.
limitation: These are retrospective scouting labels, not a live pre-snap prediction. Some zone schemes include matching players.

question: Who might rush unexpectedly?
data: scouting: Pass Rush role, positionLinedUp; tracking: pre-snap location
method: In replay, highlight players annotated as pass rushers and show how many rushed. Let the host reveal the roles after the snap.
limitation: This reveals recorded roles after the fact. Predicting a surprise blitz before the snap needs a separately validated model.

question: Why was a receiver left so open?
data: tracking: all players; plays: coverage type
method: Replay defender movement alongside the receiver's spacing curve and coverage label.
limitation: No defensive assignments, communication or playbook. Do not automatically flag a blown coverage.

question: Did one receiver create space for another?
data: tracking: route runners and defenders; scouting: roles
method: Show two selected receiver trails plus defender movement around their crossing/diverging paths.
limitation: Movement supports a host's explanation; it cannot prove a decoy caused a defender's decision.

question: Did the defense change shape after the snap?
data: tracking: frameId, x, y, ball_snap; plays: coverage label
method: Use synchronized snapshots at snap and release, or animate coverage players' trails.
limitation: The play-level coverage label does not describe a time series. A second inferred label requires a classifier or manual annotation.

question: Which matchup is a team exploiting?
data: Missing target IDs and defensive coverage assignments; nearest-player positions are available
method: A limited descriptive version tracks distance to a manually selected defender on selected plays.
limitation: Nearest defender is not coverage responsibility. Receiver-vs-corner target rates need more labels.

question: How fast was that player moving?
data: tracking: s, frameId, nflId
method: Display s in yards/second or multiply by 3600/1760 for mph. Take the maximum only over the chosen tracked interval.
limitation: This is maximum observed speed in the available segment, not necessarily whole-play speed.

question: How did the runner find a gap?
data: The data covers passing/dropback plays, including some QB scrambles; no designed-run sample
method: A selected QB scramble can show movement within available frames. General running-lane analysis needs rushing plays and fuller tracking.
limitation: Do not evaluate running backs or designed rushing schemes with this passing subset.

question: Was that run better than expected?
data: Missing representative rushing plays, handoff context and expected-rushing model
method: Add rushing data and an independently validated model before using this metric.
limitation: The scramble subset is not a substitute for the population of rushing plays.

question: Was a gain mainly the runner's work or blocking?
data: No contact-event labels, full rushing tracking or broken-tackle charting
method: Requires contact annotation plus end-of-run outcome and replay evidence.
limitation: Player proximity is not proof of physical contact. Cannot apportion credit from current fields.

question: Could a defender have stopped the runner?
data: Missing consistent post-catch/rushing tracking, tackle opportunities and missed-tackle labels
method: Add complete pursuit sequences and reviewed tackle labels; then show angles or model opportunities.
limitation: Current data is useful for approaching the QB, but that is not a general tackling model.

question: How did a player escape or get caught?
data: tracking: x, y, s; event run or qb_sack when present
method: Show a selected QB's escape/approach sequence inside the observed interval. For receivers, show separation creation before release.
limitation: Most catch-and-run escapes cannot be reconstructed. End the animation where source frames stop.

question: Should the team go for fourth down, punt or kick?
data: Available: down, distance, field position, score, clock; missing: complete play-by-play, kick outcomes, timeouts, model
method: Display the situation as context. Decision recommendations need conversion, field-goal and downstream possession models.
limitation: This passing-only sample is selected by the actual decision taken. It cannot fairly estimate all options.

question: How far should the offense advance to justify going for it?
data: Same missing decision models as fourth-down recommendations
method: Draw the actual first-down target now. Add an analytical go-for-it boundary only after developing a calibrated decision model.
limitation: The first-down line is a rule-based target; a go-for-it boundary is a different quantity.

question: Is the team close enough for a field goal?
data: Field position available; no kicker, field-goal attempts, weather or kick model
method: Can show distance to the end zone. A kicker-specific success zone needs additional kicking data and a probability model.
limitation: Do not fabricate a universal kick range or display a probability from field position alone.

question: Can the trailing team still come back?
data: Pre-snap scores and clock available; timeouts, full possession sequence and model absent
method: Show score deficit and recorded game clock. A probability or possession forecast needs supplemental data and a validated model.
limitation: Do not turn score/time into an unvalidated comeback percentage.

question: Can the leading team run out the clock?
data: Quarter, down and gameClock available; timeouts, all plays and clock-state details absent
method: Display known context only; supplement full game state before determining kneel-out conditions.
limitation: Missing timeout and possession details change the answer materially.

question: How important was that play?
data: playResult and before-play state available; no EPA, WP, reliable complete after-state or fitted model
method: Show recorded yards and outcome today. EPA/WP require supplemental values or models with the correct state transitions.
limitation: Yards gained is not EPA; next CSV row is not necessarily the next play.

question: Why is one team winning?
data: plays: passResult, result, down, coverage; scouting: pressure labels
method: Compare the included passing/dropback sample: completions, sacks, pressure-labelled plays and coverage splits, with denominators.
limitation: Cannot produce full-game yards/play, turnover count, rushing efficiency, drives or scoring rates from this subset. Review nullified and penalty-affected records before official-stat aggregation; 489 descriptions contain No Play.

question: Is this player having an exceptional game?
data: players and per-play roles/outcomes across 2021 weeks 1-8
method: Compare a clearly defined passing/blocking metric within the supplied sample, showing sample size and period.
limitation: No complete career, season or current-player baseline. Avoid best/worst rankings without adequate samples and comparable roles. Review nullified and penalty-affected records before official-stat aggregation.

question: Was that a catch, touchdown, fumble or penalty?
data: plays: passResult, playDescription, foulName1-3, penaltyYards; selected tracking event labels
method: Display the official recorded outcome and recorded penalties. Creator can explain them using available movement context.
limitation: No ball height, body/foot contact detail or video. Cannot independently adjudicate catches, goal-line possession or penalties.
